2027-04-02.title: First Friday of Resurrection: the Feast of Martyrs
2027-04-02.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The prayer of Azariah in the furnace
The ancestors who bore witness by faith
2027-04-02.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta). The Feast of Martyrs: in the East Syriac tradition the Friday after Easter is the feast of all the saints, the martyrs and confessors (verify locally). It is also the First Friday of the month. There is no abstinence on this first Friday after Easter. The calendar notes the fuller passages: Daniel 3:25–45, Acts 6:8–7:10, Hebrews 11:3–10, 32–12:2 and Matthew 10:16–33. The prayer in the furnace belongs to the Greek part of Daniel 3, and Bibles number these verses differently.
2027-04-02.verse: Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven.
theo: On the first Friday after Easter the Church of the East keeps the feast of all the saints, and above all of the martyrs. The placing is deliberate. The martyrs are those who went with Christ through death into life, and so their feast belongs in the week of the Resurrection, not in the gloom of a funeral. The East Syriac tradition explains the day by its own history. In the fourth century the Persian king Shapur II launched a long persecution against the Christians of his empire. Mar Shemun bar Sabbae, Catholicos of Seleucia-Ctesiphon, refused to betray his flock or to worship the sun, and by tradition he was put to death on Good Friday, about the year 341 or 344, together with a great company of bishops, priests and faithful. Since Good Friday could not become a feast, the martyrs came to be remembered on the Friday after Easter: so the tradition tells it. The Church of St Thomas in India received this calendar and this memory, and the Syro-Malabar Church still keeps the day as the Feast of Martyrs. The witnesses have not stopped. Blessed Rani Maria Vattalil, a Franciscan Clarist sister from Pulluvazhy in Kerala, was stabbed to death on a bus near Indore in 1995, killed in hatred of the faith, stirred up by her work among the poor, and was beatified in 2017. Her family later forgave the man who killed her, and he came to their home to ask their pardon. A martyr's blood, and a martyr's family's forgiveness, preach the Resurrection more loudly than any sermon.

The first reading takes us into a furnace. Three young Jews in Babylon, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, have refused to worship the golden statue. Before they are thrown into the fire they give the king an answer that every martyr has repeated: “If our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the furnace of blazing fire and out of your hand, O king, let him deliver us. But if not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods and we will not worship the golden statue that you have set up.” (Daniel 3:17–18). Then the astonishing scene: “They walked around in the midst of the flames, singing hymns to God and blessing the Lord.” Azariah stands still in the fire and prays, and his prayer is not a complaint but a confession: “Blessed are you, O Lord, God of our ancestors, and worthy of praise; and glorious is your name forever! For you are just in all you have done.” He does not accuse God of injustice; he accepts that his people have sinned and still trusts in God's mercy. The king, looking in, sees four men walking unbound in the fire, and the fourth looks like a son of the gods. Many Fathers saw in that fourth figure the Son of God, who does not take his witnesses out of the fire but walks with them in it. This is how the martyrs have died: singing, forgiving, and not alone.

In Acts we meet the first Christian martyr. “Stephen, full of grace and power, did great wonders and signs among the people.” Some members of one synagogue in Jerusalem argue with him, “But they could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke.” False witnesses are found to accuse him of speaking against the Temple and the law. Stephen was himself a Jew, as were the apostles and the whole first community; the quarrel was within one family, and the Church, following the Second Vatican Council (Nostra Aetate 4), never reads such passages as a charge against the Jewish people. What Luke wants us to see is the face of the witness: “And all who sat in the council looked intently at him, and they saw that his face was like the face of an angel.” Like Moses coming down from Sinai, Stephen's face shines because he has been with God. Soon he will see heaven opened, pray for his killers and die (Acts 7:56–60). The Letter to the Hebrews then opens the great roll of the witnesses of faith. “By faith Abel offered to God a more acceptable sacrifice than Cain's... he died, but through his faith he still speaks.” By faith Noah built the ark. “By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to set out for a place that he was to receive as an inheritance; and he set out, not knowing where he was going.” These men and women did not see the promise fulfilled, “For he looked forward to the city that has foundations, whose architect and builder is God.” The martyrs are the ones who believed the city was real enough to die for.

The Gospel is Jesus' instruction to witnesses. Three times he says, Do not be afraid. “So have no fear of them; for nothing is covered up that will not be uncovered.” “Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul.” “So do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows.” The reason is the tenderness of the Father: “Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground apart from your Father. And even the hairs of your head are all counted.” Then the promise and the warning: “Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven; but whoever denies me before others, I also will deny before my Father in heaven.” The Syriac word for martyr, sahda, like the Greek martys, means simply a witness. Few of us will be asked to die for Christ, but all of us are asked to acknowledge him: at the office table, in the hostel, in the family group chat, in the way we do business and the way we speak of the poor. Today is also the First Friday, the day many families give to the Sacred Heart. The Heart that was pierced on the Cross and rose glorified is the source of every martyr's courage. To keep this feast well is to ask for a little of that courage, and to make one small act of acknowledgement before the day ends.
conn: The fourth man in the fire.
“When you walk through fire you shall not be burned” (Isaiah 43:2); the king sees four men walking unbound in the furnace (Daniel 3:92, in Catholic numbering); “I am with you always” (Matthew 28:20).

Moses' face shone because he had been talking with God (Exodus 34:29); Stephen's face was “like the face of an angel” (Acts 6:15); at the Transfiguration Jesus' face “shone like the sun” (Matthew 17:2).
The first martyr prays as his Master.
Jesus prays, “Father, forgive them” and “into your hands I commend my spirit” (Luke 23:34, 46); Stephen prays, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit” and “do not hold this sin against them” (Acts 7:59–60).
The roll of faith in Hebrews 11 ends with “so great a cloud of witnesses” (Hebrews 12:1); John sees a great multitude “robed in white, with palm branches in their hands” (Revelation 7:9).
“Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his faithful ones” (Psalm 116:15); “the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God” (Wisdom 3:1).
“Blessed are you when people revile you and persecute you” (Matthew 5:11); “they have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony” (Revelation 12:11).
altar: From the earliest centuries the Holy Qurbana was offered over the tombs of the martyrs, and relics of saints are still placed in our altars. The martyrs gave their bodies for Christ because Christ first gave his Body for them; at the altar their sacrifice is joined to his.
Each time we receive Communion we say Amen to the Body of Christ in front of everyone. It is the smallest act of witness, and the martyrs began with the same Amen.

live: Make one quiet act of acknowledgement today: say grace in a public place, or speak of your faith when the subject comes up.
Pray today, by name if you can, for a country where Christians are suffering for their faith.
Go to the Sacrament of Reconciliation or make an act of reparation to the Sacred Heart today.
Pray Stephen's prayer for one person who has hurt you: Lord, do not hold this against them.
fathers: Aphrahat the Persian Sage, Demonstration on Persecution (in substance)

Writing during the persecution of Shapur, Aphrahat recalled that the righteous have always been persecuted: Abel by his brother, Jacob by Esau, Joseph by his brothers, Moses by Pharaoh, David by Saul, Daniel by the satraps, the three young men by Nebuchadnezzar. Last of all Jesus was persecuted and crucified. So the Church should not be surprised by suffering; she walks the road of the righteous, and her Lord walks it before her.

It is not the punishment but the cause that makes the martyr. Many suffer, but the martyr suffers for Christ and for the truth. Let us honour the martyrs by imitating their cause, not by seeking their pain, and by loving the One for whom they died.
magis: Martyrdom is the supreme witness given to the truth of the faith; the Church has carefully gathered the records of those who persevered to the end.
Communion with the saints joins us to Christ; we venerate the martyrs and saints as disciples and imitators of the Lord.
In the yearly cycle the Church commemorates the martyrs and saints, proclaiming the Paschal mystery in those who suffered and were glorified with Christ.
Hebrews 11 celebrates the faith of the ancestors; Abraham is the model of obedient faith.
Before Pilate Christ bore witness to the truth; the Christian must not be ashamed of testifying to the Lord.
saints: 2 April: the Feast of Martyrs. The East Syriac Churches remember on this Friday all the martyrs and confessors, among them Mar Shemun bar Sabbae, Catholicos of Seleucia-Ctesiphon, and his companions, put to death under the Persian king Shapur II in the fourth century (by tradition on Good Friday, about 341 or 344; verify locally how your eparchy keeps the day).
2027-04-02.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, first-born from the dead and faithful witness, you walked with the three young men in the fire and showed your glory to Stephen as he died. We thank you for all the martyrs and saints of your Church, for Mar Shemun and his companions, for the witnesses of our own land and our own time. Give us their courage to acknowledge you before others, their faith to go out not knowing where we are going, and their love to forgive those who hurt us. With Mary, Queen of Martyrs, who stood beside your Cross, let us one day join the great multitude robed in white. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Daniel: if God delivers us, good; but if not, we will not bow down. The young men walk singing in the fire.
Acts: Stephen, full of grace and power, faces false witnesses with the face of an angel.

2027-04-02.action: Make one small public act of acknowledgement of Christ today.
2027-04-02.question: Where am I tempted to keep quiet about Christ, and what would it cost me to speak?
kidsaint: He was the chief bishop of the Christians in Persia about 1,700 years ago. The king ordered him to make the Christians pay a double tax and to worship the sun. Mar Shemun said he would not hurt his people and he would worship only God, the Maker of the sun. He was put to death together with many priests and believers, on Good Friday, the story says. Lesson: a good shepherd stays with his flock and stays with Jesus!
2027-04-02.special: First Friday of Resurrection: the Feast of Martyrs (All Saints in the East Syriac tradition). First Friday of the month. No abstinence today.
term: The Syriac word for a martyr, meaning ‘witness’, like the Greek martys. Kerala Christians know it from the name of Mar Geevarghese Sahada, St George the Martyr. Every Christian is called to be a witness; some are asked to give that witness with their blood.

family.explain: Jesus said that tiny sparrows are sold very cheaply, but God sees every one of them. And he even counts the hairs on your head! So we do not need to be afraid. Long ago some brave Christians, called martyrs, loved Jesus so much that they would not stop following him even when bad people hurt them. Today we remember them. We can be brave too: we can tell our friends that we love Jesus, and pray even when others are watching.
family.intention: We pray for Christians in places where it is dangerous to follow Jesus, that God may keep them brave and safe.
family.ask: Ask: “When is it hard for me to say that I belong to Jesus?”

illus: A first-year engineering student from Kottayam shared a hostel room in Pune with three boys from other states. On his first Friday evening he went to a corner of the room, made the sign of the cross and began the night prayer his grandmother had taught him, almost in a whisper. One roommate laughed; another filmed it on his phone. For a week he prayed in the bathroom. Then he remembered the Gospel he had heard at the Feast of Martyrs: Do not be afraid. The next night he prayed in the room again, out loud. Nobody filmed it this time. Before the end of the term one of the roommates, who had not been inside a church since he was a child, asked if he could come along to the Holy Qurbana on Sunday. ‘You did not argue with us,’ he said. ‘You just kept praying.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, faithful witness, we gather with the great cloud of witnesses who surround us. Give us their courage and their joy. Amen. Alleluia!
share: But if not, we will not serve your gods (Daniel 3:18). Would my faith hold if God did not give me what I ask?
His face was like the face of an angel (Acts 6:15). Does my face show that I have been with God?
He set out, not knowing where he was going (Hebrews 11:8). Where is God asking me to step out in faith?
Everyone who acknowledges me before others (Matthew 10:32). Where can I acknowledge Christ this week?
interc: For Christians persecuted for their faith in every land, that the Lord may walk with them in the fire.
For the Church of the East and all the Churches of the Syriac tradition, heirs of the martyrs of Persia.
For those who are mocked or excluded at school or at work for their faith, that they may not be afraid.
For those who have hurt us, that we may forgive them as Stephen forgave.
For our dear departed, that they may join the saints in the city whose builder is God.
pm.close: Father, precious in your sight is the death of your faithful ones. Through the prayers of the martyrs and all the saints, keep us faithful, make us brave, and bring us to the city that has foundations. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, on the first Friday after Easter the Church of the East remembers all the saints and above all the martyrs. They belong in Easter week, because they went with Christ through death into life. Our tradition remembers Mar Shemun bar Sabbae and the martyrs of Persia, killed, the story says, on a Good Friday long ago. And our own Church has given witnesses in our own time, like Blessed Rani Maria, whose family forgave the man who killed her.

In Daniel three young men face the furnace and say: our God is able to save us; but if not, we will still not bow down. That ‘but if not’ is the heart of faith. We do not love God only for what he gives. And in the fire they walk and sing, and a fourth man walks with them. Christ does not always take us out of the fire, but he never leaves us alone in it.

Stephen, full of grace and power, is dragged before the council on false charges. Stephen was a Jew, like the apostles; this is not a story against any people. It is the story of a witness whose face shines like an angel's, who sees heaven open and prays for those who stone him. He died as his Master died: forgiving.

Hebrews reminds us of the long line of witnesses. Abel, of whom it is written, “he died, but through his faith he still speaks.” Abraham, who “set out, not knowing where he was going.” They lived for a city they did not yet see. So did the martyrs. So must we.

Jesus says three times: Do not be afraid. Your Father sees every sparrow, and he has counted the hairs of your head. And then: “Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven.” Most of us will not be asked to die. But every day we are asked to acknowledge him: at work, in college, in the family chat, in how we treat the poor.

Today is also First Friday. Let us go to the Heart of Jesus, pierced and risen, and ask for a little of the martyrs' courage. And before tonight let us make one small act of witness. Christ is risen! Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, today we remember the martyrs. They were brave friends of Jesus who would not stop loving him, even when they were hurt.
Jesus says: ‘Do not be afraid! God counts every hair on your head.’ Let us be brave and say: ‘I love Jesus!’

opts.a: The whole family of the saints
intro: In our Church the first Friday after Easter is the feast of the martyrs and of all the saints. It is a family feast: the Church in heaven and the Church on earth together.

sub: The souls of the righteous are in God's hand.
points.apply: Learn the life of one saint this Easter season.

points.h: The saints of our own soil
sub: Let us now praise famous men.
points.apply: Pray at the tomb or shrine of a saint of our Church, or ask their intercession at home.

sub: Chosen before the foundation of the world.
points.apply: Choose one practical step toward holiness this week.

concl: We are surrounded by a family of witnesses who pray for us.
Their feast is our call: we too are called to be saints.
opts.resolve: This Easter season I will learn the life of one saint and take one practical step toward holiness.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, in the joy of Easter our Church keeps the feast of the martyrs and of all the saints. Why now? Because the saints are the fruit of Easter. Christ's victory over death is seen first in those who followed him through death into life.

The Book of Wisdom says: the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment will ever touch them (Wisdom 3:1). Hebrews tells us that we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses (Hebrews 12:1). We do not run the race alone. The saints are not far from us. They are our elder brothers and sisters, cheering us on and praying for us.

Sirach says: let us now sing the praises of famous men, our ancestors in their generations (Sirach 44:1). Our Church has its own family of saints: St Alphonsa, St Kuriakose Elias Chavara, St Euphrasia, St Mariam Thresia, Blessed Rani Maria and many others. Hebrews says: remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith (Hebrews 13:7).

But this feast is not only about them. God said to Israel: you shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy (Leviticus 19:2). Paul says God chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love (Ephesians 1:4). Holiness is not for a few special people. It is the vocation of every baptised person, in the kitchen, the office and the field.

So let us thank God today for the saints, especially the martyrs. Let us learn the life of one saint this season. And let us take one practical step toward holiness, so that one day we may join them in the great feast of heaven, of which every Holy Qurbana is a foretaste. Christ is risen! Alleluia! Amen.

intro: Stephen, the first martyr, died praying for his killers. At his feet lay the coats of the witnesses, and a young man named Saul was watching. The blood of martyrs is the seed of the Church.

points.h: False witnesses and the true witness
points.apply: Refuse to join in gossip or false accusation this week.

points.h: Lord, do not hold this sin against them
points.apply: Pray daily this week for someone who has hurt you.

sub: The grain of wheat that dies.
points.apply: Pray for Christians persecuted today, and support them in some practical way.

concl: The martyr's strongest word is forgiveness.
God makes the blood of witnesses the seed of new life.
opts.resolve: This week I will pray for one who has hurt me and for persecuted Christians.
homily: Dear friends, in today's reading Stephen, full of grace and power, is accused by false witnesses who say he speaks against the holy place and the law (Acts 6:13). The Psalm had prayed: false witnesses have risen against me (Psalm 27:12). The world has often answered the truth with lies.

The word martyr means witness. Stephen bore witness not only with his words but with his face: all who sat in the council saw that his face was like the face of an angel (Acts 6:15). Later, as they were stoning him, he knelt down and cried out: Lord, do not hold this sin against them (Acts 7:60).

In the Old Testament, the priest Zechariah was also stoned in the court of the Lord's house, and as he died he said: may the LORD see and avenge! (2 Chronicles 24:22). Stephen prays differently, because he has learned from Jesus on the Cross. The martyr's greatest victory is not to die bravely, but to die forgiving.

And here is the surprise. The witnesses laid their coats at the feet of a young man named Saul, and Saul approved of their killing him (Acts 7:58; 8:1). Stephen's prayer was answered in that very man, who became the Apostle Paul. Jesus had said: unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit (John 12:24). That day the Church was scattered, and the word spread everywhere.

Today many Christians still suffer for their faith. Let us pray for them and help them. Let us refuse to join in false accusations. And let us pray every day this week for someone who has hurt us, as Stephen did. Then we too will be witnesses of the risen Lord. Christ is risen! Alleluia! Amen.

intro: Theme: “Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven.”
The young men in the fire, Stephen with the face of an angel, the witnesses of faith, and the call to fearless witness.

sub: The fourth man in the fire.
q: If our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the furnace of blazing fire and out of your hand, O king, let him deliver us. But if not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods and we will not worship the golden statue that you have set up.
But they have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, for they did not cling to life even in the face of death.
points.apply: Tell God in prayer today that you will trust him even if he does not give you what you are asking.

q: Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone because he had been talking with God.
And all who sat in the council looked intently at him, and they saw that his face was like the face of an angel.
points.apply: Spend time with God before a hard conversation, and let him be seen in you.

q: Go from your country and your kindred and your father's house to the land that I will show you.

Therefore, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight and the sin that clings so closely, and let us run with perseverance the race that is set before us.
points.apply: Ask one saint or martyr to be your companion this Easter season, and learn their story.

q: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven.
points.apply: Make one small public act of witness today: grace before meals, a word of faith, a sign of the cross.

concl: The martyrs went with Christ through death into life, and he walked with them in the fire.
We are surrounded by their cloud of witnesses; let us not be afraid to acknowledge him.
2027-04-02.resolve: Today, make one act of public witness, pray for a persecuted Church by name, and forgive one person with Stephen's prayer.
